reason: Re-opened packet.js veda 56 --verse 5.85.6. Sāyaṇa glosses māyām as prajñām (wisdom), then: it must not be said that the work from spreading the mid-air to the unfilled sea befits Parameśvara alone and not Varuṇa, tasya varuṇādirūpāvasthānāt (since He abides in the forms of Varuṇa and the rest). The entry’s ‘fitly Varuna’s, since the Supreme Lord abides in the forms of Varuna and the other gods’ follows the Sanskrit exactly; Wilson’s note inverts it (dropping na vācyam), and the entry rightly does not follow Wilson there. Evidence found verbatim. Plain sense checked in day.js: 5.85.7 and 5.85.8 plead for sins to be removed, so ‘before the hymn turns to pleas for pardon’ holds. verse.js ok [438,6]; entry-check ok, 44 words; revision 209192 dated 2019-08-11. No school, comparison or tone issue.
